Biography

Ethan Gladys Norma is a stooped pale young man from the small metropolitan nobility, with noble subtle traits, clever eyes and a gun on his cheeks. He sat on a tiny stool to the left of Adrian's throne and recorded the emperor's words. When he met Mira in the spring of 1774, he called himself the third secretary of His Majesty, and in the "One Star" he was already the fifth secretary. (Minerva; Only One Star) Ethan didn't stutter, but he paused a little bit between the first sound and the rest of the word. He knew almost everything about Faunterra and the first families of duchies and counties, he was well versed in painting and wore a sword. He secretly served as a protection agent for Mark. (The Protection) Mark considered him one of the most useful agents and the most intelligent of those who trusted. According to him, the real advantage of the stutter was "fluffy, marshmallow innocuity": none of the nobles did not take Ethan seriously.

In "Arrow, Coin, Spark"

Acquaintance

Mira, posing as Gloria Northwood, met Ethan at the palace library. At first, he answered her questions monosyllabically, "Yes, milady," and said only that he would invite her to a dance. When the archivist reported that Baron Rosbet, heir to the throne, had died of the plague overnight, Ethan admitted that the disease did not kill so quickly. He told the girl about the patronage and how many people were captured after the Shutov plot, and tried to warn her against a dangerous investigation. (Jesters' Conspiracy) Mira burst into flames, but, already leaving, he returned and invited her to the celebration of the northern azalea in the garden of Lumini, where the cousin of the lord Sir Adamar visited. Later, Mark admitted that Ethan made a “grave mistake” when he began to frighten her with secret guards at the first meeting, and was sure that she understood him at the same time.

In the garden Lumini Ethan was a gallant and even too warning gentleman. He paid for the entrance, talked about fellow nobles and helped Mira to make sure that the simple-minded Ser Adamar was a bad conspirator. Then he admitted that he wanted her to give up the search: the rest of the heirs are far away, and the jester Manson adores the lord. He did not believe that the emperor wanted to kill, because "there is only one star", and all the life of Faunterra revolves around Adrian. At the ball, he told Mira that she was "alive", stood up for her before Alanis Almera's ridicule and explained why the emperor was holding on to an alliance with the Duke of Almera: he supports reforms that no one likes.

Search for Layla Talmir

Ethan waited an hour in the heat outside Mira's house to accompany her. She asked to postpone the promised visit to the Amber Gallery and go with her to Linden Square, where Leila Talmir once lived. From there they went to St. Teresa's almshouse. There Ethan tried to question the sick, and when a crowd of beggars surrounded Mira, he grabbed the sword and, pushing them, led her out into the street. A real servant of Leyla Ashby caught up with them and suggested the way to Pale Meadow. Later, Mira, deciding that she had picked up a liver disease in the hospital, wrote to Ethan to make him appear as a doctor immediately. He thanked me and assured me that he was healthy.

Recognition

June 27 at the summer games Ethan, blushing and going astray, confessed to Mira in love:

"Lady Gloria, I love you!"

She cut him off with a cry of "Shut up!" because at that moment she was struck by a guess about Ayden Almera's plan. (Aiden Almera) Mira wrote a note to a street copyist and sent Ethan to take it to Mark. When she later asked what he was saying to her, Ethan replied, "So, about nonsense." Mark soon told Mira that Ethan was serving in the patronage, and that the post of secretary was just an excuse to be under the ruler, and that Ethan was asking permission to visit her. After learning that the "modest, shy, caring" secretary is a spy of the secret guard, Mira refused.

The “Soul of the West”

When "Gloria" was suddenly taken from the capital, Ethan came to Rebecca Litland and asked where she was going, "not for his majesty - for himself." Becca showed him a friend's farewell letter. It was Ethan who told her that Gloria had been “taken away,” and Becca pondered the word.

In "Only One Star"

Doubts

Ethan didn't believe Gloria had gone to the convent. He wrote Mark three notes, which he burned: “Never write such nonsense.” Ethan argued that the farewell note was cold and devoid of her irony, that Countess Sybil did not look like a mother who lost her daughter, and that she for some reason sent Gloria's security guard, Sire Vanden. Mark ridiculed his feelings, but Ethan reminded him of his own lesson: any strangeness should attract attention. He even asked Sybil herself. At the celebration in honor of the car "waves" Ethan pointed out to Mark how pleased the Countess, although the rise of the bride of the lord is not at all beneficial to her. Sybil said, "Mark, call off the puppy." Meanwhile, Ethan helped Mark investigate the missing letters from the archive and the murder of a printing worker. His joking remark that the document can be snapped and set on fire, led Mark to a guess.

When Erwin Origin rebelled, Adrian sent the disgraced Mark to the First Winter, formally assuring the transfer of power, and in fact killing Erwin. Ethan, according to the emperor, no longer had a place in the secretariat, and he had to accompany Mark. Mark offered to leave, but Ethan referred to His Majesty's order and guessed that Mark had a role for him. He played the role of Lady Gloria.

Change of Bride

On the way to the First Winter, Mark and Ethan drove to Elena's boarding house in the Lake. (Elena-by-the-Lake Boarding School) Lady Theodora's stewardess exhibited them, but Ethan pleaded that Gloria was the victim of a conspiracy, and this interested the mentor Martha Valeria. While Mark questioned the students, Ethan kept records, and the girls looked at him unceremoniously. In the gallery of graduates Ethan recognized on the portrait with the sign “Gloria Sybil Dorina... Northwood" the face of the bride is Minerva Stagforth. That's how the switch opened up. Stunned, he muttered, “Did she... lie to me?” Martha Valeria ordered them to flee immediately and gave them horses. On the way, Ethan admitted that he knows where the real Minerva is. Becca deciphered her note: the one at Ulyana Sad's monastery in the west of Almera. But Ethan realized that Mark was right: you can take the girl from the monastery only by order of the emperor. "You've grown by ten years," Mark said. Ethan begged his superior not to go to the First Winter for certain death, but that night the kairs intercepted both.

On September 6, 1774, in the First Winter, Ethan tried to explain that they had come to certify the legality of the transfer of power. Mark sent him to bed, and Erwin ordered him to set aside a regular bedroom. Mark Erwin took for questioning, and to assure the legality instructed Ethan: “I bet he had no poison. And he is a noble.” The freed Ethan from the Southern Way sent a report to the emperor. According to this letter, Adrian exposed the substitution and arrested Sybil and Gloria Northwood at the court.

Salvation of the World

On Adrian's special orders, Ethan, along with Lieutenant Shatterhand and a detachment of the Azure Guard, tracked down Mira. In the monastery of Ulyana, they found out who took her away, and secretly arrived in Waymar. Ethan replaced one of the two actors in the hoods, who played the kidnappers in a terrible play of a wandering troupe - for agate - and so penetrated the castle and saw Mira among the audience. The unit could not get into the castle with weapons. Then the guards began to monitor those who enter the castle and leave it, and noticed that Martin's "Jeggers", dressed in hunting, circuitous ways go to the ruins. The stolen watch told the rest. In November 1774, the unit broke into the torture cellar of Martin Shayland. Upon learning Mira, Ethan was horrified at her appearance and introduced himself: "Ethan Gladys, the Lord's secretary. Do you remember me?" He walked around and supported her. When on the road they were intercepted by Iona's detachment with Seymour Steel's keel, Ethan tried to pass the rescuers off as mercenaries from the Iron Hand Brigade.

On the ship, Ethan brought food and tea to Mira, straightened the blanket and persuaded her to go down to the cabin, and then threatened that he would sleep on the deck next to her. He, together with Shatterhand, solemnly informed her of General Alexis' victory at Pixie and spread a pre-arranged map of the South Road on the blanket. At Fliss, he brought her chrysanthemums. Reviving Mira scratched her face on the frosting of the window and asked Ethan to check if anyone was watching her from the window. Ethan shamed the lieutenant for rude soldier stories and assured Mira that she would write novels. In Aleridan, Ethan and Shatterhand decided to wait for the emperor. Their units lived apart so as not to attract attention. When Mira realized that Gallard's privateer was behind the intrigues, she demanded an urgent meeting with Ethan: she wanted to know whether he and Mark had reported to the emperor about the participation of the privateer in Sybil's plot. Shatterhand considered the meeting reckless, because Ethan's squad could not escape from surveillance, but promised to arrange it. Interfere with the people of the parish, who came for Mira to the hotel. Upon learning of Adrian's "death", Ethan was among those who surrounded Minerva when she recognized herself as the legitimate empress.

In "A Doll on the Throne" and "The Voice of Winter"

Searching for body

After the coronation, Minerva considered Ethan one of the few old friends. (Minerva's Coronation) However, from Shatterhand, she learned that Ethan was in Almer with protection agents. A protocol officer from the Imperial Secretariat was required to search for Adrian's body, and Ethan himself asked the Lord Chancellor to entrust it to him, but did not want to nurse Minerva's wounds. Erwin later said that he sent Ethan on purpose: he is loyal to both Minerva and Adrian, and if there is a catch in the death of the lord, he will find him. Erwin expected Ethan to discover the truth and hide it from him. Ethan and Captain Hyder Leed, with a hundred greys and a hundred agents, combed the banks of Beck for thirty miles, picked up ninety-two corpses and identified two hundred and sixteen dead on the train. Ethan was involved in identifying the body. He was the first to tell Erwin that Martin Shayland almost killed her Majesty, and demanded to bring the villain to the imperial court.

Leed reported to the Duke that Ethan had not stumbled anywhere, but "holds on to his bosom" some idea. Erwin put the Voice of Winter on the table and questioned Ethan with a sword in his hand: whether he had found Manson, whether Adrian was alive, why he so easily believed in the death of his beloved master. Ethan turned pale, but he said it was all in the report. Erwin first told him to put him in a stone bag, but when Leed asked for permission to "use methods", he cut him off: no, just in prison, without walking, for bread and water.

Torture

In the spring of 1775, Minerva thwarted Erwin's massacre on the Holy Field, and then sent him a snowdrop flower with a ribbon: "You are not the lord, my lord. (Standoff at the Holy Field) Come to terms." The enraged Duke ordered to gather her men and tell Leed: “Let him shake Ethan out of everything. in any way.” The torture occurred in early May. Under torture, Ethan gave out his find: the Eternal Hilt on the corpse was inserted into the sheath incorrectly. On this basis, Erwin realized that the body did not belong to Adrian.

The “Yanmei Hunt”

In the negotiations, Minerva demanded Ethan be returned to her, and Erwin lied that he would return "in a week or two" after completing his assignment. Lord Desmond reproached his son with rumors that he had "eliminated some secretary Ethan", and Erwin burst into flames:

“Ethan is a little sucker, a jerk, a nothing!”

Asked if Ethan was still alive, Leed assured the Duke that he was "almost in good health" and suffered no irreparable damage. At Manson's trial, Minerva asked where Ethan was. (Trial of Manson) Leed replied that the agent had left Faunterra for personal reasons. Finally, in the House, Erwin publicly named Ethan the man he had sent to Back, and announced that "having put some pressure on Ethan," he had learned of the inverted Hilt. (Chamber of Representatives)

In "Humans and Gods"

At night, Mark brought Minerva to Ethan's parents' house in the Emilia area, where the petty official nobility lived. The elderly couple rejoiced that their son could eat semolina today. Mark pulled the sheet off, and Mira, seeing a disfigured Ethan, rushed to the window, as once in Waymar's basement. Mark explained why he showed it to her. Ethan suffered because Adrian decided to hide, not to give up: the pride of the ruler is paid by ordinary people with their pain. Mira left Ethan a note. Since then, she has been managing his health every day and sending doctors she and Raven paid for. She explained to Manson that she did not go to Ethan herself, because she would only spoil his unrequited feelings. Mira reproached Mark that he used the truth about Ethan as an excuse for manipulation.

Robert Origin handed Minerva a healing item from Erwin. Mira in anger asked if the Duke "apologized for Ethan" because he knew she couldn't talk to the Objects. Robert shrugged his shoulders. He listed, "Well, hand, well, teeth, well, skin...", Ethan will live to old age. Robert suggested that Hyder Leed, who considered Ethan "virtually whole", did not bother the Duke with such trifles. Minerva later demanded to take her back to Ethan, now in the afternoon, to apologize for not appreciating his loyalty for a long time. Sending Becca to dangerous negotiations with Steppe Fire, Minerva thought, "Another Ethan" is a hard, painful, but the only right decision. (Rebecca Litland)

The Shadow of the Great Tree

In July 1775, Minerva asked Navi to cure Ethan in debt for the Gauntlet of Power. Looking at him, Navi said, “Very bad.” Within two months, the bones had fused incorrectly, and they could only be corrected by destroying and fusing again. It would be a real torture: the subject-scalpel gave only local anesthesia. Navi estimated the success at sixty-seven percent and warned that in about one in eight cases, a nerve node could be damaged and the facial muscles paralyzed. The parents refused to torture their son again. Mira begged Ethan to agree, remembering the yard last spring, but he covered his face with his palm and shook in silent sobbing. Mira realized that her visits in the halo of imperial glory were only a shame and humiliation for the cripple, who, perhaps, still loves her. For all her visits, he said only “your”, “greatness” and “sorry”.

“Your Majesty, I am sorry. I'm not worth the trouble..."

Mark then tried to persuade Ethan for treatment, but, according to him, he “does not believe in anything.” Mark told Navi that Ethan “refused to heal himself out of stupidity.” In the main cycle, Ethan no longer appears.

In "Fantasies"

In Fantasies, which the author calls possible futures, Ethan serves Adrian as a secretary in a white mask. In the Device, he is not named, but all the signs indicate him, and in the Ad-ri-an! Adrian says directly to him, “You have the word, Ethan.” In the story "The Device" (March 1776), Adrian, who recognized himself as the mayor of Faunterra, serves as a personal secretary in a white mask. Relatives and friends said that he can be proud of the injuries received, “defending the honor and freedom of a great man.” He himself hoped that “broken bones” would grow and the world would become the same, and then he would remove the mask. The secretary stuttered a little at the first sounds of words. Once he confessed to Minerva in love, and she missed the confession by ear. Therefore, he did not accept healing “from her hands”: her late care humiliated him. Blondes he did not trust from the day he met the former Duchess of Almera, that is, Alanis.

In the town hall, the secretary introduced ceremonies, honors and a protocol that is not inferior to the palace, and “ripped out” the efficiency of the former lady-burgomaster. He selected correspondence for Adrian and noted the bookmarks of the article in the university “Bulletin”. So the lord learned about the recording device of Nicholas Ollie. The secretary met Ollie and his assistant Alice Cavendish at the town hall. He noted that Ollie admires Minerva, because “there was a time when he himself said this about this woman.” He believed that Minerva betrayed both him and her emperor, and therefore asked Backfield to establish surveillance on Ollie and Alice: they could contact the First Winter. (Croydon Beckfield)

"Ad-ri-an!"

In November 1776, on the opening day of the House, the secretary in a white mask entered the hall following Adrian and General Joseph Gore. When Adrian declared the election annulled and demanded an oath from the lords, only Gore and the "white mask" rose, and both followed him through a breach in the wall. In the evening, at dinner at the Palace of Pen and Sword, Adrian said: "Thank you, General. You have the floor, Ethan.” The secretary, stuttering, reported that "the news in the right light" was transmitted to the "Voice of the Crown" and the Branch of the Forefathers: "The L-lords betrayed the lord again and tried to kill again." He also said that the order of the lord was transferred to the management of rail roads and the branch of Faunterra - Arrowback was de-energized. After the death of Adrian Minerva, she weeping, thought that she had pushed everyone who loved her away, and among them she named Ethan.

Personality

Robust, delicate, verbose in letters and courtesies, Ethan was smart, observant and persistent. He did not consider himself entitled to argue with the noble lady, but for the sake of Mira he went against both Mark and Bear. He remained carelessly loyal to Adrian and Minerva, did not break in front of Erwin's sword and tried to hide his find even from the Leed Wolves. Countess Sybil, who had married Miru at Gallard's side, mockingly asked whom she would choose, giving her free rein: "Secretary Ethan or Lord Adrian?" The world blushed, "as if caught on hot." She never responded to Ethan's feelings.

Trivia

  • In Shadow of the Great Tree, Minerva recalled believing that Ethan and Shatterhand had sent Adrian, her "protection and guiding star" to Waymar for her.
  • Before the decisive operation against Paul, when Navi wanted to confess her feelings to Minerva, she remembered Ethan and his recognition in the capital arena.
  • In early media outlets, Mir, making amends for going to the hospital, did visit Ethan in the Amber Gallery: he showed himself as a connoisseur of painting and explained to her how the secretariat makes up the queue of applicants for Saturday receptions. In the edition of 2026, this scene is not - the visit to the gallery remains postponed.
  • At the beginning of A Doll on the Throne, Minerva named Ethan among the "tiny handful of old friends" along with Shatterhand.
